newsitem.title: USA: Matria says study shows positive results.
newsitem.headline: Matria says study shows positive results.

text.p: Matria Healthcare Inc Wednesday said a randomized clinical trial showed significant improvements in pregnancy outcomes when home uterine activity monitoring (HUAM) was used by high-risk expectant mothers.
The study, which was conducted at three academic research institutions, was published in the current issue of the "American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology."

In the study, 339 women at risk for preterm birth were randomized to receive either standard high risk prenatal care alone or high risk care with the addition of twice daily HUAM. The group receiving HUAM experienced a 41 percent reduction in their incidence of preterm birth and a 50 percent reduction in admissions to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). Infants born to mothers in the HUAM group spent a total of 469 fewer days in the NICU compared to their non-monitored counterparts.
In comparison with non-monitored women, the women in the monitored group also had longer gestations and delivered infants with greater birthweights.
A number of previous studies on home uterine activity monitoring reported pregnancy outcome data only on the subgroup of patients who experienced preterm labor, leading to criticism of those studies.

Nearly 400,000 infants are born prematurely in the U.S. each year. Currently, over 5 million hospital days per year are spent treating prematurity and over $5 billion are spent each year on neonatal intensive care.
Matria is the leading national provider of comprehensive obstetrical homecare and maternity management services to HMOs, indemnity carriers and employers.
